title: What is known about 1RB0RC_1LC1RE_1RA1LD_0LC0LA_1RF1RD_---0RD
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB0RC_1LC1RE_1RA1LD_0LC0LA_1RF1RD_---0RD.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. Its tape is mostly two blocks: an alternating block (10)^x and a solid block 1^y. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. Lean proves no halt in the first 10,000 steps by the kernel alone and in the first 107 with native_decide; the C simulator finds no halt in the first 109 steps; an exact macro simulator (blocks of 2 cells) finds no halt in the first 1015 steps.

What Lean proves. The whole frame map: 8 tape shapes, 78 cases, each proved for all sizes by a symbolic run (next_sound), and the cases where the map is undefined halt (none_halts). So the machine halts from blank tape if and only if the map, iterated from the frame the run reaches after 2 steps, reaches one of those cases (halts_iff). By native_decide the first 108 frames (about 4.5·1011 machine steps) do not. Whether the orbit ever does is open.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (F0); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 4,302 cells have been visited and 3,792 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: power/power
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.321). Right of the start it grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.347).

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>15</sup> steps
claims.text: An exact macro simulator (blocks of 2 cells) runs 1015 steps without a halt. The macro simulator cuts the tape into blocks of K cells, run-length codes them, and crosses a whole run at once when the head leaves it on the far side in the state it entered with; it agrees with the plain simulator tools/c/tmrun cell for cell.

claims.title: Two blocks trading length
claims.text: At the moments the head reaches a new cell between steps 9.79·10<sup>7</sup> and 9.94·10<sup>7</sup>, the tape is an alternating block and a solid block plus a few cells, with lengths (806, 336), (672, 604), (540, 874), (722, 513).

claims.title: The halting state, seen from the run
claims.text: In the first 10<sup>8</sup> steps state F was entered 83,257 times, always reading a 1 (F0 halts).

claims.title: The frame map agrees with the machine on a grid
claims.text: For each of the 8 frames and every canonical choice of sizes below 16, the machine reaches exactly the frame, sizes and step count the fitted map predicts (30,736 frames, py/framemap.py verify 16). The map is now proved in Lean; this check is how it was found.

claims.title: The frame map agrees with the run
claims.text: Run from blank tape next to the machine, the fitted map predicts the whole tape at each of the 48,691 frames in the first 5·106 steps (py/framemap.py real 5000000).

claims.title: The whole frame map
claims.text: next in lean/Phases.lean sends each of the 8 frames to the next one the machine reaches, in 78 cases; next_sound proves every case for all parameters, each from a symbolic run in lean/Pieces.lean (generated by py/pieces.py) glued by tape_eq. Where next is undefined (.z 1 1 1, .w l 0 1, .w l 1 0, .W l 0 1, .W l 1 0) the machine halts (none_halts).

claims.title: Halts if and only if the map reaches an undefined case
claims.text: init_start: the run from blank tape reaches Ph.z 0 0 2 after 2 steps. halts_iff: the machine halts from blank tape if and only if some iterate of next from there is a frame where next is none.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>8</sup> frames
claims.text: no_halt_phases, by native_decide: the first 108 iterates are defined. By the step counts of the fitted map (py/framemap.py run 100000000) that is about 4.5·1011 machine steps.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. Its tape is an alternating block and a solid block whose lengths trade back and forth; each pass rewrites one block into the other.

facts.text: No halt in the first 10<sup>8</sup> frames of the frame map proved in Lean (about 4.5·10<sup>11</sup> machine steps).
It halts if and only if the frame map, iterated from the first frame, reaches a frame where it is undefined.
No halt in an exact macro simulator (blocks of 2 cells).
An alternating and a solid block trade length.
No halt, proved in Lean; the first 10,000 by the kernel alone.
No halt in the C simulator; 4,302 cells visited.

sections.heading: What the machine does
html: Stop the machine whenever its head first reaches a new cell. With a for 10, around step 9.8·107:

• step 97,915,409: D>0 a^2 1 a^802 1^338 (left end)
  • step 97,921,865: A>0^2 a^806 1^336 (left end)
  • step 98,376,215: 1^2 a 1^604 a^672 C>0 (right end)
  • step 98,837,298: A>0^2 a^540 1^874 (left end)
  • step 99,362,025: C>0^2 a^722 1^513 (left end)

The tape is two long blocks, one alternating and one solid, and at successive moments their lengths trade: 806 copies of 10 and 336 ones, then 604 ones and 672 copies of 10, then 540 and 874, then 722 and 513. Rewriting a block of length x costs about x passes of length x, so the width grows like the cube root of the step count. The shape is the one of the three machines 1RB1RD_0LC1RA_…_1RF0LD_---0RE, where one block doubles at the other's expense; the exact rules here have not been worked out.

sections.heading: Where a halt would have to come from
html: The halting transition is F reading a 0. F is entered only from E reading a 0 (1RF), so a halt needs E>0 0. In the first 108 steps F was entered 83,257 times, every time on a 1, and 82,807 of those times at least 7 cells from the left end.
Whether the trading ever leaves E in front of two 0s is open.

sections.heading: The frame map in Lean
html: The frames (blank tape outside; X is the head in state X on the next cell; u^v is v copies of u, so 11^L is 2L ones; a frame counts only at a moment where the head turns round):

• z: 1^L 10^j C 1^R
  • y: 1^L A 10 10^j 1^R
  • w: 1^L C 00 10^j 1^R
  • u: 1^L 10^j 1 A 00 1^R
  • Z: 1110 1^L 10^j C 1^R
  • Y: 1110 1^L A 10 10^j 1^R
  • W: 1110 1^L C 00 10^j 1^R
  • U: 1110 1^L 10^j 1 A 00 1^R
The map next (Lean names; each variable a natural number):

The map was found by fitting the machine's runs (py/framemap.py) and collapsing the fit into cases (py/pieces.py); Lean then checks every case for all sizes. It is undefined only at .z 1 1 1, .w l 0 1, .w l 1 0, .W l 0 1, .W l 1 0, and those halt. So the open question is exactly whether the orbit of Ph.z 0 0 2 reaches one of them; the first 108 frames do not.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.321). Right of the start it grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.347).
After 109 steps the tape spans 4,302 cells (2,289 left of the start, 1,181 right), with a density of 1s of 0.881.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

family: doubling between an alternating and a solid block
summary: Its tape is an alternating block and a solid block whose lengths trade back and forth; each pass rewrites one block into the other.
